name: Ansible world-writable file mode / readable tmpfiles
attack_scenario: any unprivileged local user edits the world-writable config or script Ansible just deployed (privilege escalation via a root-run cron/service reading it), or reads secrets left in world-readable become tmpfiles during a privilege-drop task
negative_test_hint: as an unprivileged local user write "pwned-by-unprivileged-user" into the deployed file and assert the write is denied because the file is not world-writable

exemplar.explanation: A file/copy/template mode whose final octal digit carries the write bit (for example 0777, 0666, or 0002) makes the deployed file world-writable, so any unprivileged local user can tamper with configs or scripts that a root-run service or cron later reads. allow_world_readable_tmpfiles: true similarly leaves privilege-escalation temp files readable by every local user; restrictive modes such as 0640 keep writes limited to owner and group.
